Purpose: Main processor. One board runs everything: pitch-detection DSP on core 0, display and UI on core 1. PSRAM for the audio buffer; two I2S peripherals so the mic and amplifier run at the same time. Uses 19 GPIO of 44.
Captures the instrument for scale detection and tuning. Digital I2S output, so no analog front-end.
Shows the detected tonic, scale and sargam. Round format suits the tuner dial, taal cycle and circle-of-fifths views.
DAC and amplifier in one part so the processor drives the drone and metronome click directly.
Reproduces the drone and click, sized to fit inside the 70mm enclosure.
Sets tempo, pitch and mode. Friction-coupled to the knurled bezel so the whole ring turns.
Pulses the beat so the player feels time instead of hearing it. Usable in an ensemble or under headphones.
Charges the cell over USB-C with over-charge, over-discharge and over-current protection.
Roughly 8 hours of untethered use. 34.5 x 51 x 6.3mm with a JST-PH 2.0 connector, so it fits inside the 70mm x 22mm puck.
Validate the full circuit and firmware before committing to a PCB.

ONE ESP32-S3 is used, not three. The previous link pointed at a 3-pack listing (now out of stock), which is why the parts list looked like it needed three processors. The design needs 20 GPIO and both I2S peripherals, which one S3 provides with room to spare. Pin map is in the README. Select the N8R2 or N16R8 variant on the listing; either works.

Several parts are sold only in multipacks. 'Unit price USD' is the pack price divided by pack size; 'Qty used in build' is the real board count. Line totals are what actually gets charged at checkout, since the whole pack must be bought.

All ten links were checked live on 14 Aug 2026 and were in stock at the prices shown. The EC11 6-pack is the single most expensive line at 32.98 USD; a smaller pack would cut it substantially if one is in stock at order time.

This is the PROTOTYPE BOM and it funds build phases 1-3: breadboard bring-up, accuracy measurement, and all four modes working. It is deliberately breakout modules, not bare ICs, so the firmware can be proven before any board is ordered.

The PCB design in docs/ is phase 4 and uses bare parts that are NOT in this list: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 module, TP4056 SOP-8, TLV62569 buck, XC6206P332 LDO, AO3400A MOSFETs, USB-C 16P, JST-PH and JST-SH connectors, and passives. That is a separate and later spend, costed at about 31 USD per unit at quantity 5.
